 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 08-03-2023, at about 10.15 a.m., the petitioner was carefully riding her two-wheeler bearing No.KA-51-EX- 4899, on NICE road towards Kanakapura road,
by following traffic rules and regulations.
When she reached near Unity Gate, due to white topping, there was slow movement of vehicles.

At that time the driver of tipper bearing No.KA-51- A-9014 came from back side of petitioner on her right side, in rash and negligent manner and suddenly turned his vehicle to his left without giving any signal or indication and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner and ran over the right foot of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has sustained severe degloving crush injuries to her right foot.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Cauvery Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident she was working as Head - Operations at M/s Creditai Fintech Private Limited, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.1,12,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Thalaghattapura Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said tipper for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-, with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.

On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted that, the tipper lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9014 was insured by it under the Policy No.VGC0450038000106 and the same was valid from 01-03-2023 to 29-02-2024.
Further, it has admitted its liability subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that, at the time of alleged accident, the rider of two-wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-51-EX- 4899, without holding driving licence and being incompetence to ride the said vehicle, rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the insured tipper lorry bearing No.KA-51-A-9014 and caused the alleged accident.
The same is substantiated in the spot mahazer and sketch drawn by the jurisdictional police.
The damages stated in M.V.A. report clearly substantiate that there is gross negligence on the part of the rider of the two-wheeler bearing No.KA-51-EX-4899.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 08-03-2023 at about 10.15 a.m., on NICE Bannerghatta road, near Unity Gate, Thalaghattapura, Bengaluru City, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51- A-9014 ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.

What order or Award ?

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement tipper bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A-9014 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondents No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the scooter bearing No.KA-51-EX-4899 and she herself has dashed to the tipper bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-A-9014, which was proceeding in the same direction and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of said tipper.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any evidence, nor it has produced any document to establish the above contentions.
Even, the respondent No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

In such circumstances, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that,
the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the scooter bearing No.KA-51-EX-4899.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending tipper bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A-9014 and dashing the same to the scooter of the petitioner.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the scooter or there was any contributory negligence on her part, in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 40 feet wide Bannerghatta-Kanakapura road, near Unity Gate, NICE road, Thalaghattapura, Bengaluru city, in between the offending tipper bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-A-9014 and scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-51- EX-4899 of the petitioner, which was proceeding in the same direction.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-EX-4899, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending tipper bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A- 9014 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

Admittedly, the said final report/charge- sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-A-9014.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending tipper lorry bearing Reg.

18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending tipper lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A-9014 and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained right forefoot, midfoot and sole degloving injury with crushed and fracture of all toes,
complete fracture of 2nd to 5th metatarsal bones.

Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.23.
As per Ex.P.23, the date of birth of the petitioner is 29-12-1987.
The accident has taken place on 08-03-2023 at about 10.15 A.M.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 35 years.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered right forefoot, midfoot and sole degloving injury with crushed and fracture of all toes,
complete fracture of 2nd to 5th metatarsal bones and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgeries.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical impairment to the extent of 35% to the right lower limb.

The Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 to 13 discharge summaries, Ex.P.28 case-sheet, Ex.P.29 OPD record, Ex.P.30 x-ray and Ex.P.39 clinical records also clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and for the said injury she has undergone surgery.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
He has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 08-03-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 05-02- 2024, which is after lapse of ten months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the five toes of the petitioner are amputated, the fracture of other bones are united and the wounds are completely healed.
Further, he has clearly admitted that, he has assessed physical disability and not functional disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, the disability assessed by P.W.3 at 35% is with respect to right lower limb and he has not assessed the physical disability to the whole body.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 15%
to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.

Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15%
to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

20. The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was working as Head - Operations at M/s Creditai Fintech Private Limited, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.1,12,000/-
per month.
Further, she has deposed that, due to the accidental injuries she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.

To substantiate the same she has produced appointment letter, pay slips for the month of November-2022 to September-2023, leave certificate, termination letter, bank statement, letter of appointment, leave certificate, termination letter and information letter, which are marked as Ex.P.16 to 20 and 31 to 34.
Further, she has also examined the authorised person/Director of CreditAI Fintech Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru, as P.W.4, to prove her avocation and income.

The P.W.4 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner was working as Chief Operation Officer in their office since 01-05-2020 and she was a permanent employee, she was on leave from 08-03- 2023 to Shubham Khushlani vs Subramani.R on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90667713/
7 30-04-2023, she resumed her work from 01-05- 2023, due to partial amputation of her right leg,
she could not fulfill her job responsibilities satisfactorily, hence on 10- 10-2023, they terminated her from employment due to non- performance and as on the date of accident her gross salary was Rs.1,12,000/- per month.
The Ex.P.18 leave certificate clearly speaks that, due to injuries sustained in the accident she has availed medical leave from 08-03-2023 to 30-04-2023 and she has resumed her work from 01-05- 2023.
Further, as per Ex.P.19 termination letter, due to non- performance she has been terminated from the job with effect from 10-10-2023.
This clearly goes to show that, the petitioner has lost her job due to injuries sustained in the accident in question and as such she has suffered loss of future income.

As per Ex.P.17 salary slips for the month of November-2022 to September-2023, the petitioner was drawing gross salary of Rs.1,12,000/- per month and after deducting professional tax of Rs.200/-, she was drawing net salary of Rs.1,11,800/- per month.

Therefore, the income of the petitioner as on the date of accident is held at Rs.1,11,800/- per month,
which comes to Rs.13,41,600/- per annum.

21. As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 35 years is 16.

22. Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.8,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 27 medical bills, as per Ex.P.15.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.5,54,423/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,54,423/- under the head of medical expenses.
23. Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.,
forefoot, midfoot and sole degloving injury with crushed and fracture of all toes, complete fracture of 2nd to 5th metatarsal bones and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgeries.

As per Ex.P.10 to 13 discharge summaries (total 4), the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 8 days, from 08-03-2023 to 09-03-2023,
14-03-2023 to 15-03- 2023, 23-03-2023 to 24-03-2023 and 29-03-2023 to 30-03- 2023, in Kauvery Hospital, Bengaluru and Nypunya Aesthetic Clinic, Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.3 the said injury has caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injury sustained and the disability suffered by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.80,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
24. Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.10 to 13 discharge summaries (total 4), the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 8 days in Kauvery Hospital, Bengaluru and Nypunya Aesthetic Clinic,
Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 8 = Rs.8,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.

26. Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Flat No.317, 'B' Block, Radiant Shine Apartments, Beguru- Koppa road, Beguru, Bengaluru, the accident has taken place on Bannerghatta towards Kanakapura road, near Unity Gate, NICE Road, Thalaghattapura, Bengaluru City and she has taken treatment at Kauvery Hospital, Bengaluru and Nypunya Aesthetic Clinic, Bengaluru.

Taking into consideration the distance in between the place of accident and the above hospitals,
compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
27. Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 8 days as in-patient at Kauvery Hospital, Bengaluru and Nypunya Aesthetic Clinic, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by her.
Further as per Ex.P.18 lave certificate, she was on leave for 53 days from 08-03-2023 to 30-04-2023 and as per Ex.P.20 bank statement, she was drawn the salary for the said period.
Therefore, she is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of income during treatment period.
28. Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 35 years and unfortunately she has sustained forefoot, midfoot and sole degloving injury with crushed and fracture of all toes, complete fracture of 2 nd to 5th metatarsal bones.
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 15% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
29. Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner require to wear customised silicone prosthesis for her right foot for entire life.
The approximate cost of cap mould right foot silicone prosthesis is around Rs.1,00,000/-, it needs periodical maintenance and has to be changed every year.
She is advised for laser treatment for the scars over the thigh and foot, she may need around 25 sittings, each sitting will cost Rs.6,000/-.

To substantiate the same,
the petitioner has produced quotation, which is marked as Ex.P.14.
She has also examined the Marketing Manager of KARE Prosthetics and Orthotics as P.W.5.
Further, the P.W.5 has clearly stated in his cross-examination that, the total cost of silicone full foot prosthetics for right foot of the petitioner is around Rs.86,000/-.
The life of prosthesis is around 6 months to 2 years and she required change at around 20 to 25 times in her lifetime.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- to the petitioner, towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

31. Liability:

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.9, the driver of offending vehicle by name L. This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
At that time the driver of tipper bearing No.KA-51- A-9014 came from back side of petitioner on her right side, in rash and negligent manner and suddenly turned his vehicle to his left without giving any signal or indication and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner and ran over the right foot of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has sustained severe degloving crush injuries to her right foot.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Cauvery Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident she was working as Head - Operations at M/s Creditai Fintech Private Limited, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.1,12,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Thalaghattapura Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said tipper for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
